title: Bold words, sudden retreat
odia:
ଏସା କରେଙ୍ଗା
ତେସା କରେଙ୍ଗା
ସିପାହୀ ଦେଖିଲେ ଶୋଇ ପଡ଼େଙ୍ଗା।
literal_meaning: “I will do this, I will do that”—but at the sight of a soldier, I will lie down.
meaning_odia: କଥାରେ ବହୁତ ସାହସ ଦେଖାଇବା, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅସଲ ପରୀକ୍ଷା ଆସିଲେ ଡରି ପଛେଇଯିବାକୁ ଏହି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କହେ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଦୁଇ ପଦର ବାହାଦୁରି ଶେଷ ପଦରେ ଭାଙ୍ଗିଯାଏ।
explanation: The speaker announces one bold action after another, then becomes timid as soon as a soldier appears. The inspected Odia Vasa gloss identifies the target as someone who claims fearlessness in words but loses courage when action is required. The ending punctures the earlier boast.
usage_example: Someone loudly promises to challenge an unfair decision, but falls silent when the person responsible arrives. The saying could tease that gap between promise and action. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: Hindi-influenced କରେଙ୍ଗା and ପଡ଼େଙ୍ଗା rhyme around the Odia phrase ଦେଖିଲେ ଶୋଇ. The repeated boasts build momentum, and the last line abruptly turns confident speech into a picture of retreat.

odia_summary: କଥାରେ ସାହସ, କାମ ବେଳେ ଭୟ—ଏହି ବିରୋଧକୁ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ।
english_summary: Boastful courage disappears when it is put to the test.
